approachQuestion.prompt:
Packing Whole Tiles

An h by w board has blocked and open cells. Cover every open cell exactly once with unlabelled 1 by 2 dominoes, horizontal or vertical. Return all tilings, each represented by its pairs of cell coordinates. Domino order is irrelevant; return each tiling once in any order. Empty open area has the single empty tiling.

Examples:
board=["..",".."] -> two tilings: both horizontal or both vertical.
board=[".#"] -> [].
board=["##"] -> [[]].

Constraints: 1 <= h,w <= 6; at most 24 open cells. Input is a row-major board; # is blocked and . is open.

options.text: Find the first uncovered cell, try each domino covering it with an uncovered neighbor, and undo both occupied cells on return. Emit only when the board is fully covered.
options.feedback: Every complete tiling has exactly one domino covering the first uncovered cell. This canonical anchor removes alternative orders of placing the same dominoes.

options.text: Place the first legal domino found and continue without revisiting that choice.
options.feedback: On board=["...",".##"], taking the top-left horizontal domino strands the bottom-left cell, but taking the left vertical domino leaves a valid top-row horizontal domino.

options.text: At each step choose any uncovered adjacent pair and emit every completed placement list.
options.feedback: On an open 2 by 2 board, placing the top horizontal domino before or after the bottom one emits the same tiling twice.

options.text: Generate coverings by choosing any uncovered adjacent pair, normalize each completed placement list, and deduplicate them in an ordered set.
options.feedback: This is correct but explores redundant placement orders; fixing the first uncovered cell prevents those duplicate branches.

feedback.reason: Every complete tiling has exactly one domino covering the first uncovered cell. This canonical anchor removes alternative orders of placing the same dominoes.
details: Copy occupancy into a working board. At each call scan row-major for the first uncovered cell. If none remains, copy the placement list. Otherwise try pairing that cell with each uncovered orthogonal neighbor, mark both, recurse, then undo.

Choose the first uncovered cell as a canonical next decision; every complete tiling must pair it with one uncovered neighbor. This avoids permuting the order of placing identical final tile sets. Restore both cells after each branch.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze `acm-b18-07-search` only. Let N=h*w, V count all recursive calls, S count all cell inspections in first-uncovered scans, and R count all coordinate records copied into returned tilings. Use a copied N-cell occupancy board; each call checks at most four neighbors. Choose the tightest stated time and auxiliary-space pair. Count recursion and mutable working state; exclude supplied input and returned output storage, but include copying work in time. Primitive integer/index operations and preallocated-array updates cost constant time; dynamic appends are amortized constant time. No hashing is used unless explicitly stated.

options.text: O(N + V + S + R) time, O(N) auxiliary space
O(N + V + R) time, O(N) auxiliary space
O(N + V + S + R) time, O(V) auxiliary space
O(N² + R) time, O(N) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Include board scans per state, neighbor trials, and placement-list copies.
details: Copying occupancy costs N; each call has constant neighbor overhead and a scan accounted for by S. Output copying adds R. These are exactly the performed categories of work.
The occupancy board has N cells; the path and stack have at most N/2 dominoes/frames.

Let N=h*w, V count all recursive calls, S count all cell inspections in first-uncovered scans, and R count all coordinate records copied into returned tilings. Use a copied N-cell occupancy board; each call checks at most four neighbors.
“O(N + V + R) time, O(N) auxiliary space”: Finding the first uncovered cell requires the scans counted by S.
“O(N + V + S + R) time, O(V) auxiliary space”: The search tree is not retained; only the occupancy board and active path are stored.
“O(N² + R) time, O(N) auxiliary space”: The number of partial coverings can be exponential, even on a fixed board area bound viewed parametrically.
